paragraphs.source_en: What Chaya Shirōjirō had said was true. As Kanpaku Hidetsugu left Jurakudai and made for Fushimi, Hideyoshi drew five thousand troops from Fushimi Castle and the surrounding districts and sent them out to meet him. Hidetsugu had prepared only a single palanquin, and his attendants could be counted on one hand—apart from the pages Fuwa Bansaku, Yamamoto Toneri, Yamada Sanjūrō, and Saika Otora, there was only Ryū Seidō, an eloquent scholar; not one senior retainer showed his face.
